Adopt mirtverse for your course

Source: vignettes/articles/adopt.Rmd
adopt.Rmd

mirtverse comes with a complete, free set of materials for a course on item response theory. You can adopt all of it, or take one lab for a single class. Everything is open and editable, and it runs on student laptops.

What you get

Material What it is Where
Sample syllabus A 12-week graduate syllabus with outcomes, schedule and grading, ready to edit Word · PDF
Book One chapter per week, with worked examples and exercises with solutions; also as PDF and EPUB Read online
Ten labs Interactive cases with live mirt models, learning goals, timing, discussion prompts and an answer key Teaching labs
Course map Week-by-week readings, code, labs and datasets, plus versions for 8-week, undergraduate and second courses Course map
Instructor toolkit Labs on your own data, editable copies of the labs and chapters, checks before class Toolkit
AI in measurement module Four weeks (book chapters 13 to 18, Labs 7 to 10) or a one-day workshop AI Hub
Handouts Two-page cheat sheet, a model-choice poster and a glossary of nearly 90 terms Cheat sheet · Which IRT model? poster · Glossary

Adopt it in four steps

  1. Download the sample syllabus (Word) and fill in the bracketed parts. Each week names its book chapter and lab.

  2. Check the setup on a lab computer a week before class:

    install.packages("mirtverse", repos = c("https://okanbulut.r-universe.dev", "https://cloud.r-project.org"))
library(mirtverse)
list_labs()
run_lab("model-choice")

  3. Send students the setup page, Start here: New to R, which walks through installing R, RStudio and mirtverse.

  4. Tell us you are using it (next section), so you hear about updates and the course can be listed below.

Tell us you’re teaching with it

Fill in the short course form (a GitHub account is needed). It takes two minutes, and it shapes what gets built next: New labs, chapters and datasets come from instructors’ requests.

To hear about new releases, open the GitHub repository, choose Watch, then Custom, and tick Releases. You will get one email per release and nothing else.

Courses using mirtverse

Courses whose instructors agreed to be listed will appear here. Be the first: add your course.

Citing the materials

If you use the book or labs in published teaching materials, please cite the book (10.5281/zenodo.23885605) and the package (citation("mirtverse")).
